title: Nonstructural Carbohydrates in Italian Ryegrass Determined by Liquid Chromatography
source_location: J-STAGE article abstract; methods and reported ranges
geography: Experimental location is not stated in the accessible abstract
material: Italian ryegrass herbage (Lolium multiflorum), sampled at varied growth stages including aftermaths
measurement_method: Freeze-dried, milled grass was extracted with 80% ethanol; mono- and disaccharides were determined by liquid chromatography. Fructosan was determined from hot-water extract using anthrone colorimetry.
evidence_class: Primary literature measurement ranges; class B for source observations
license: No explicit open-reuse license identified on the publisher record. This repository extract contains limited numeric facts and provenance metadata, not the article text or figures; verify rights before redistribution beyond this project.
activation_state: Reference ranges remain class B source evidence. The glucose, fructose, sucrose, and fructosan ranges are used only as allocation weights in a separately classified class-C GreenHub proxy that partitions the Smit roadside-grass aggregate. No range midpoint is presented as a measured GreenHub value.
limitations: The source material is cultivated Italian ryegrass, not the GreenHub Dutch roadside-grass sample.
The abstract gives ranges across growth stages and aftermaths, not per-stage means, SDs, replicate counts, or a probability distribution.
The resulting GreenHub species split is a literature-based cross-study allocation; it is not an assay of the July 2026 VARTA sample.
The original aggregate extractive-sugar pool and the literature species ratios come from different studies; sensitivity and matched monosaccharide analysis remain appropriate.
